transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-04 10:00 PT | Duration: ~72 minutes | Attendees: Avery Chen, Nina Rao, Samir Patel, Lina Gomez, Ethan Brooks, Maya Thompson + all staff

Summary: Avery opens with a quick state of the business, then product leadership runs through Dedicated, Private, Optimize updates; engineering covers reliability SLOs and key infra work; HR briefs on hiring guidance; 20 minute Q&A at end.

[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone, good morning, afternoon depending on where you are. thanks for joining our November all-hands. i know it's a busy week so i'll keep the opening short. overall, top line, we're tracking towards Q4 revenue plan but need to be mindful of cost and churn, particularly across a few mid-market accounts.

[00:34] Nina Rao: quick from infra, we've seen the kernel perf improvements land on the staging Dedicated pool. initial numbers look like 8-12% lower latency p50 for 2k token sequences when the new attention kernel runs, but there's still tail jitter at burst loads.

[01:12] Speaker 3 (Samir?): yeah, the results are promising. we still want to validate under realistic workloads - multi-tenant bursts, mixed-length sequences - before flipping the rollout. will run an extended soak this week.

[01:40] Lina Gomez: on product, Dedicated demand is healthy; sales is seeing a steady uptick in proof-of-concept requests especially from fintech and health-care verticals. Private deployments also picked up - a couple of larger deals in EMEA that want VPC + HSM integration.

[02:05] Ethan Brooks: quick commercial color, revenue pipeline is strong but long. a few large deals are in procurement/legal and that's pushing close timelines. we're coordinating with product and security to get the required docs over the line.

[02:40] Maya Thompson: headcount posture - we are instituting a temporary hiring pause on most non-critical roles. exceptions include security, core infra, and revenue-critical hires. we'll publish guidance in the next 48 hours.

[03:05] Avery Chen: appreciate that context. we want to be clear about the tradeoff: protect runway while continuing to deliver on the highest-impact product work. lina, can you walk through the product roadmap bullets?

[03:28] Lina Gomez: sure - three bullets for Q4: 1) Dedicated resiliency and autoscaling improvements (canary rollout in Dec), 2) Private: enterprise onboarding flow + KMS/HSM integrations, 3) Optimize: better quantization recommendations and a new batching advisor in console.

[04:10] Nina Rao: adding to Dedicated point - the autoscaler prototype now supports policy-based scaling by latency SLO. initial internal tests show a 15% improvement in meeting p95 under steady-state, though peak cost still needs tuning.

[04:45] Samir Patel: engineering plan is to stabilize the new autoscaler with small customer pilots in late Nov, full rollout in Jan if pilots look good. important to note, the autoscaler depends on better prefix cache heuristics to avoid cold-start token spikes.

[05:20] Ethan Brooks: commercial ask - can product and eng produce a concise one-pager for sales that outlines the Private onboarding steps and approximate timelines? procurement teams keep asking for a clear schedule.

[05:48] Lina Gomez: yes, we'll do that. target 11/10 for a publishable checklist. we'll include typical timeline expectations (1-3 weeks for VPC, 3-6 for on-prem OEM style installs).

[06:15] Nina Rao: on security/compliance, SOC2 Type 2 audit is in progress - control evidence mostly collected, we expect the formal report by late November. also, KMS integrations are in staging. a note: customers asking for HSM-backed keys, we've prototyped HSM flow with one partner, still ironing out RPC retries.

[06:56] Avery Chen: thanks. i want to call out a few customer success wins - we had a large retail customer move from hosted to Dedicated this month, and they reported 2x throughput improvements for their reranking flow. nice work cross-functional.

[07:22] Speaker 7 (sales rep): question - on pricing, are we going to adjust pricing tiers for Dedicated vs hosted? there's confusion in field.

[07:40] Avery Chen: short answer: not right now. we'll issue clarifying guidance to sales on cost buckets and expected unit economics per profile. Samir and Lina, can you provide expected cost delta tables?

[08:05] Samir Patel: we'll produce an internal sheet with model archetypes and rough token-cost and latency estimates. won't be customer-facing initially.

[08:30] Speaker 9 (engineer): any news on the caching improvements? some of our customers still get cold KV cache problems.

[08:50] Nina Rao: yes, the caching team pushed a dynamic prefix caching heuristic into staging. helps for multi-session conversational apps - we've got a 20-30% hit rate improvement in early tests. more tuning needed for heterogenous workloads.

[09:20] Lina Gomez: on Optimize, we're packaging quantization recommendations as configs in the console and a suggested quant profile per model family. this helped one customer reduce Dedicated TCO by ~18% in their POC. we'll make the evaluation artifacts available to sales.

[09:58] Avery Chen: okay let's move to org updates and people. Maya?

[10:12] Maya Thompson: hiring pause details - this is temporary, review cadence weekly, exceptions are approved case-by-case. we want to preserve critical momentum in infra and security, so those reqs remain open. managers, please audit your open reqs and flag any critical roles by 11/06.

[10:45] Ava (employee question typed in chat): is there an impact to bonuses/compensation?

[10:52] Avery Chen: no changes to comp cycles or which bonuses are paid - this is about headcount control, not comp adjustments. HR will share more context.

[11:10] Q&A (selected):
[11:12] Speaker 11: what's our cadence for private deployment support post-onboarding?

[11:20] Lina Gomez: we'll provide 90-days enhanced support for initial customers, then transition to standard support SLAs. sales: note this in FAQ.

[11:46] Speaker 12: any changes to SSO/SAML or audit log retention we should expect?

[11:52] Nina Rao: audit log retention tiers will be configurable, and we plan to offer extended retention as a paid add-on. SSO improvements are in the next sprint.

[12:15] Speaker 13 (someone from product): timeline check - when will the batching advisor be in console beta?

[12:20] Lina Gomez: aiming for internal beta 11/18, public beta early December.

[12:38] Avery Chen: before we wrap - quick financials: runway extended a couple months with the cost measures we implemented; we'll still aim to hit growth targets but be more deliberate on spend. top three metrics to watch: net revenue retention, committed ARR growth, and unit cost per token for Dedicated.

[13:05] Samir Patel: last engineering note - the new instrumentation for tail latency will be enabled next week; please watch #infra-metrics for dashboards and alert thresholds.

[13:28] Ethan Brooks: final sales note - please continue to flag accounts stuck in procurement early; product/security can prioritize docs if we see a risk of losing the deal.

[13:52] Avery Chen: all right, thanks everyone. recap of next steps in chat: i'll share the deck; product will publish Private checklist; eng will post Dedicated perf notes; HR will post hiring guidance. we'll do a follow-up leadership sync next Tuesday.

[14:20] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and filler words; some product names auto-transcribed slightly off (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes appears as "K V cash"). this transcript is an export from Fireflies.ai with automated speaker detection and timestamps approximately every 30-90 seconds, edited slightly for readability but retaining conversational artifacts.
